title: site-astro coordinates SEO entity binding of 'coldstart' to 'codebase memory' across multiple surfaces
summary: The site maintains a coordinated SEO entity binding where the coldstart brand is consistently positioned as 'codebase memory' across independent surfaces: the footer tagline (home variant), blog index page metadata (title/description/og:image:alt), the public llms.txt machine-readable discovery file, and the shared Head layout's social-sharing meta tags. This binding is a search engine and social-media optimization strategy; all strings must stay in sync when brand positioning evolves.

title: site-astro coordinates SEO entity binding of 'coldstart' to 'codebase memory' across multiple surfaces
summary: The site distinguishes 'category slots' from body copy, and only category slots are governed: the title tag, hero kicker, footer tagline, llms.txt opening line, og.png kicker, and every meta/og/twitter description must carry the exact bigram 'codebase memory' and nothing may compete with it there. Positioning is memory-led with navigation second, so body copy is still free to describe navigation (the FAQ answer in index.astro says 'navigation and memory layer' and that is deliberate, not a miss). The phrase is applied to roughly six high-value slots ONLY — pushing it everywhere is keyword stuffing, which measurably reduces answer-engine visibility. Verified this session: the bigram was previously absent from every one of these slots because each generic surface pitched 'memory + navigation' as a co-equal pair, which is why npm/GitHub (one-sentence descriptions, forced to choose) were on-message while the site was not.

steps.role: home title tag, hero kicker, and the three meta/og/twitter descriptions
docs title/description/keywords — keywords must lead with the bigram, not generic 'agent memory'
home-variant tagline only; docs/blog taglines are not category slots
opening blockquote — the single highest-leverage line for answer engines
og:image:alt, which must match the og.png card text

invariants: Brand string is lowercase 'coldstart' everywhere (matches npm, CLI, GitHub, wordmark) — title tags are category-first, brand last.
og:image:alt in Head.astro and the kicker baked into public/og.png must say the same thing; changing one means regenerating the other via scripts/generate-og.sh.
